analysis.investment_thesis: Crompton is a legitimate consumer brand with improving operational momentum post-Butterfly acquisition, but at 34x trailing PE and EV/EBITDA of 22.7x you are paying a premium growth multiple for a business compounding revenue at ~10% and net profit at ~8% over seven years. FCF yield of ~3.7% (INR 635 Cr FCF / INR 17,088 Cr market cap) offers insufficient cushion against any earnings disappointment.
key_strengths: Near-zero leverage (D/E 0.05) after successfully paying down INR 1,700 Cr acquisition debt; clean balance sheet de-risks the downside
Consistent FCF generation — positive OCF in all 5 of last 5 years, averaging ~INR 690 Cr/yr FY21-25
Record EBITDA of INR 950 Cr in FY25 signals Butterfly integration is finally adding value and margin recovery is underway
key_risks: Operating margins are thin at 8% — any raw material spike (copper, steel) or competitive pricing pressure can rapidly compress earnings
Net profit in FY25 (INR 564 Cr) is still below FY21 (INR 617 Cr) — nearly five years of zero PAT growth despite revenue doubling; market is pricing in a turnaround that has yet to arrive
Finance costs spiked from INR 35 Cr in FY22 to INR 109 Cr in FY23 — integration-related costs highlight execution risk in inorganic strategy
red_flags: PEG ratio is roughly 4x (34x PE / ~8-9% earnings CAGR) — the growth does not justify the multiple
Forward PE of 27x requires ~27% earnings re-acceleration; consensus may be too optimistic on Butterfly synergies
DII holding of 65.7% means institutional selling pressure could weigh heavily if guidance disappoints
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Second-level thinking on Crompton: the market is clearly paying for the post-acquisition recovery story, but the data shows net profit grew from INR 496 Cr in FY20 to only INR 564 Cr in FY25 — a meager 2.6% CAGR over five years. Meanwhile, total assets ballooned from INR 2,752 Cr to INR 6,002 Cr. That is capital employed doubling for virtually zero incremental profit. The current quarter EBITDA uptick (INR 950 Cr) is encouraging but is priced in and then some at 22.7x EV/EBITDA.

FCF yield of 3.7% is well below my 6-8% threshold for a margin-of-safety entry. The balance sheet is now healthy and the brand franchise in fans and pumps is real, but this is a 8-10% grower priced like a compounder. Risk/reward is roughly balanced — not a disaster, not an opportunity. Wait for a meaningful pullback toward 22-24x trailing PE before building a position.
